# /usr/lib/sysctl.d/10-apparmor.conf
# Synthetic fixture shaped like `systemd-sysctl --cat-config` on Ubuntu 26.04 (vendor files only,
# trimmed; not copied from a real box). Tests append the homelab files to it.
kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns = 1

# /usr/lib/sysctl.d/10-coredump-debian.conf
kernel.core_pattern=core

# /usr/lib/sysctl.d/50-default.conf
kernel.sysrq = 0x01b6
kernel.core_uses_pid = 1
net.ipv4.conf.default.rp_filter = 2
net.ipv4.conf.*.rp_filter = 2
-net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter
net.ipv4.conf.default.accept_source_route = 0
net.ipv4.conf.*.accept_source_route = 0
fs.protected_hardlinks = 1
fs.protected_symlinks = 1
fs.protected_regular = 1
fs.protected_fifos = 1

# /usr/lib/sysctl.d/55-kernel-hardening.conf
# Hide kernel addresses from unprivileged users. Some tools read them from
# /proc/kallsyms, /proc/modules, etc), and this setting can censor the addresses.
kernel.kptr_restrict = 1

# /usr/lib/sysctl.d/55-magic-sysrq.conf
kernel.sysrq = 176

# /usr/lib/sysctl.d/55-network-security.conf
net.ipv4.conf.default.rp_filter=2
net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter=2
